set: A: the site as web pages: the six pages at rest, the application with its controls on, the message page for touch devices, and the controls at their real size

issues.where: Skills Assessment, under the introduction and beside the circular port
issues.what: The heading and copy tell me an assessment is required, but at rest there is neither an action nor a status. The port looks deliberately built into the page, but I cannot tell whether to click it, look elsewhere, or wait.
issues.fix: Put a visible Start assessment action under the introduction, or show a short readiness status there if the sequence starts on its own. Keep the port in its current site grid position.

issues.what: The card explains why the application is unavailable but leaves the visitor at a dead end, even though the desktop page offers a film alternative.
issues.fix: Add a clearly labeled Watch the film action below the message. Keep the mouse-and-keyboard gag in the copy.

issues.where: Submit action beneath the Human Verification card
issues.what: The button is isolated far below and to the right of the only field, and it switches to a centered axis after right-aligned Continue buttons. The verification and submission read as unrelated controls.
issues.fix: Give the resting form a shared action-row alignment with the earlier steps, or place Submit directly under the verification card on its grid. Let any deliberate displacement happen after interaction.

issues.where: The three blank fields in Personal Details
issues.what: The fields are aligned and readable, but the same unlabeled empty dropdown surface is used for a phone number, a date, and volume. The page gives no cue for what each control will accept or whether an initial value is set.
issues.fix: Add field-specific resting cues inside the controls, such as a phone-format hint, a date hint, and a current volume value, while preserving the matching housings and any later reveal.

issues.where: Bottom half of each of the three benefits cards
issues.what: Each card has a divider immediately after its only sentence, with a conspicuously empty row below. In the resting layout this reads like missing content rather than ordinary padding.
issues.fix: Remove the dividers and tighten the card height, or give the lower row a small purposeful label if the height is needed for the interaction.

issues.where: Top utility row, sound icon and Skip step link
issues.what: The row is unobtrusive and the text is readable, but the bare muted-speaker icon looks like an indicator more than a control, and Accept Defeat makes the escape hatch sound like another in-world trick.
issues.fix: Use an understated, legibly labeled sound toggle and make Skip step the primary utility wording; keep any joke separate from the action label.
